headline: Senators’ Chabot out 1-2 weeks with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Senators defenseman Thomas Chabot will miss one to two weeks with an upper-body injury, after he reaggravated an issue he had been dealing with in last Saturday's game against the Flyers.

Ottawa can absorb a short absence better than its 6-3-0 record might suggest, because the underlying play has been ordinary. The Senators hold 50.6 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality, so roughly an even split) so far this season, and 49 percent at five-on-five. Their goaltending has bailed them out: goalies have saved 2.2 goals more than the chances faced would predict, while the skaters have scored 3.8 fewer goals than their chances should have produced. A thinner blue line during that stretch tests a team that has been winning more on results than on territory. Special teams are the other pressure point, with Ottawa's power play generating 0.82 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.75 per game, so lost minutes in either area would show up quickly. The Flyers, who sit at 1-6-3, have been outplayed far more badly, at 38.3 percent of expected goals overall.
